Revised assessment incorporating SLOOS:
- The FOMC communication is dovish (ZLB, ongoing asset purchases, AIT framework, “transitory” inflation) and aims to keep financial conditions accommodative.
- SLOOS signals improving credit supply: banks eased standards for residential real estate (including GSE-eligible mortgages) and HELOCs; reduced minimum credit score requirements; and eased standards for consumer credit (credit cards, auto, other) and for investment-grade firms—especially at large banks. These developments support the transmission of accommodative policy to households and higher-quality corporates.
- However, conditions are not fully normalized: standards in some consumer categories remain tighter than pre‑pandemic benchmarks; foreign banks kept standards unchanged for IG firms and tightened for below‑IG firms; and some large banks tightened certain C&I policies. This unevenness tempers the overall boost.

Net: With SLOOS showing broad easing versus 2020, the balance of evidence is somewhat more positive than under the FSR-only lens, though still moderated by residual tightness and risk for lower-quality borrowers.
